title: Reserve negotiation and eviction safeguards for Dedicated capacity
creator: Mariana Patel
background: Customers with reserved Dedicated capacity have asked for stronger guarantees around how their reserved pools interact with transient bursts and preemption. Existing behaviours occasionally surface tenant-facing variability: late preemption, abrupt eviction of long-running requests, and unclear negotiation semantics when multiple reservations overlap in a zone. This PRD defines negotiation primitives for short-term burst borrowing, eviction safeguards for in-flight work, and operational controls so SREs and tenant owners can understand and tune trade-offs.
goal: Create a predictable, auditable reservation negotiation and eviction safeguard system that: 1) allows controlled short bursts over reservation for eligible tenants, 2) minimizes work lost to preemption, and 3) exposes controls and observability for operators and tenants to tune isolation vs utilization.
non_goals: This PRD does not change global billing model, introduce per-token pricing changes, or modify kernel-level execution optimizations. It does not include on-prem packaging adjustments beyond config flags.
requirements: 1) Negotiation API: server-side component to accept/reject temporary buffer requests with reasons; 2) Graceful eviction: signal protocol to running inferences to request checkpointing/soft-stop, with configurable grace windows; 3) Priority classes: implement reservation priorities and tie-break rules; 4) Audit trail: record negotiation/eviction events to tenant audit logs and Console timelines; 5) Controls: per-tenant knobs for max-burst, preemptibility, and eviction-window; 6) Backstop: automatic fallback routing to hosted compatible model variant when eviction would cause customer-visible error.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Feature gates and config flags exist in Dedicated control plane and are documented; 2) Negotiation API responds within 50ms p95 and returns structured reason codes; 3) Graceful eviction protocol allows inferences to receive a preemption notice and either checkpoint or finish within configured window; 4) Console surfaces per-tenant eviction history and active bursts with links to logs; 5) Automated integration test simulating a zone overload demonstrates <1% failed requests due to eviction when soft-stop is enabled; 6) SLO: average additional tail latency from negotiation must be <5ms for non-burst traffic.
design_notes: Design decided on optimistic negotiation with explicit tenant opt-in. Priority resolution uses numeric priority then reservoir-age tie-breaker. We will ship with two eviction modes: soft-stop (notify and allow grace window) and hard-evict (immediate preempt). Default for reserved pools will be soft-stop with a 30s window; enterprises can opt for 0s hard-evict for strict isolation.
tasks: Write Negotiation API and protobuf schema
Implement control-plane UI and API for per-tenant knobs
Runtime: add preemption hook + graceful-stop handler
Integrate audit events into Console and tenant logs
End-to-end test harness for overload and fallback routing
Update docs and runbook for SRE/Support
metrics: Primary: % of in-flight requests that complete successfully during zone contention; Secondary: negotiation API p95 latency, number of eviction events per tenant per week, mean lost work seconds per eviction, Console adoption (views of eviction history). Target: reduce failed requests due to eviction by 80% vs baseline during controlled overload tests.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal dogfood on staging with 2 pilot tenants and SRE manual failover (2 weeks); 2) Canary rollout to 5% of Dedicated tenants with feature flag for negotiation API (2 weeks); 3) 25% expansion with monitoring gates; 4) Full rollout and enable default soft-stop on newly created reservations. Rollback: toggle off negotiation and fall back to current eviction behaviour.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Negotiation increases control-plane latency — mitigate by caching recent decisions and using best-effort async logging. Risk: Tenants may misuse big burst settings causing noisy neighbor; mitigate with default conservative caps, tenant quotas, and cost-visibility in Console. Risk: Hard-evict can cause data loss in long requests — default to soft-stop and require tenant acknowledgement for hard-evict.
test_plan: Automated integration tests for negotiation edge cases (overlap, race), chaos tests simulating node eviction, and synthetic load tests to measure p95 latency and completion rate. Include manual verification steps for Console entries and audit log retention. Acceptance test documented in spec link.
notes: PM/Eng sync on 2026-03-11: agreed on telemetry schema and that early GA will not include cross-zone negotiation. Security requested only audit events, no tenant data will be embedded in negotiation payloads. Next milestone: API review with Runtime and Console teams.
